source.title: Topographic Training Concentrates Causal Circuits Without Improving Neuron Monosemanticity
source.authors: Gautam Ranka; S. Pandere; Aiden Dsouza

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, truncation, or wrong-document issue; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a training-time regularizer changes neuron-level selectivity and SAE feature-complexity measures, and reports a null neuron-level result alongside changes in circuit-level measures. It refines the claim by distinguishing neuron-level monosemanticity from SAE and circuit measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports activation-patching ratios and spatial-coherence results, but those concern causal clusters rather than the claim versions' neuron polysemanticity, so they are not included as rows. The TinyViT H3 patching ratios are likewise outside the versions tested here. Referenced results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study trains ViT-S/16 (and a TinyViT probe) on ImageNet-100 with a regularizer (TopoLoss) at several weights. It measures neuron-level class-selectivity entropy (Mu), its stated monosemanticity measure, so its results bear on V5's claim that regularization changes the share of polysemantic neurons. The result is null: Mu is flat across alpha. Its SAE L0 and dead-feature measures concern residual-stream SAE features, not neuron polysemanticity or its cause, so they do not test V3. Caveat: class-entropy selectivity is only a proxy. A neuron spread across classes need not respond to unrelated concepts, and the authors note the class basis may be too coarse.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also report that SAE-feature Mu is null (Table 5). They argue that neuron-level monosemanticity metrics are insensitive to circuit-level gains, and that TinyViT replicates H2 but not H3.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains vision transformers with a topographic weight-smoothness loss and measures class-activation entropy and SAE feature statistics; it does not apply the original neuron-feature visualization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured SAE L0 and dead-feature effects are present at ViT-S alpha = 1.0 but not reliably at alpha = 0.1. TinyViT results differ from ViT-S; the paper cautions that the comparison confounds depth, width, accuracy, and training budget. The monosemanticity metric uses ImageNet-100 class labels as its concept basis.

fits_no_version.finding: At alpha = 1.0, SAE L0 falls 11% and the dead-SAE-feature fraction rises 19-fold. At alpha = 0.1, L0 rises (+32.5). TinyViT L0 falls 2.1% (single seed). The L0 drop is partly accuracy-confounded (R2 = 0.72).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topographic training regularization reduces SAE-measured feature density in vision transformer residual streams without changing neuron-level selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-selectivity Mu of SAE features is also flat across alpha (0.021, 0.021, 0.026), with zero features above 0.3 (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time topographic priors do not increase class selectivity of SAE-recovered features.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-16 class-activated neuron sets are 2.79x more causally sufficient than random sets at alpha = 1.0, versus 1.68x at baseline, and more spatially clustered (Tables 1-2). TinyViT peaks at 1.42x.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topographic loss concentrates causal mass into spatially local neuron clusters.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
record.problems: The study uses a single dataset, ImageNet-100. The SAE L0 result has an accuracy confound (reported R2 = 0.72 for L0 regressed on validation accuracy; the authors say an accuracy-matched ablation is future work). TinyViT results use one seed and cannot isolate scale or depth. The authors note that class-based Mu may miss features crossing class boundaries. No results establish that the measured low selectivity reflects unrelated semantic inputs.
record.rows_left_out: H3 causal-patching ratios and spatial-coherence measurements were left out because they measure cluster-level causal sufficiency and spatial arrangement, not neuron polysemanticity or the versions' named behavior. H3 results are in Table 1 and Figure 2; spatial coherence is in Table 2.

untested.parts: No neurons are shown responding to semantically unrelated inputs. Low class selectivity is not shown to reflect unrelated concepts.
There is no test that polysemantic neurons arise from features outnumbering neurons. SAE L0 on residual outputs does not address the causal claim.
There is no test of initialization or noise producing polysemanticity when capacity is sufficient.
Only TopoLoss in ViTs is tested. SoLU, other activations and convnets are not tested. The 'without large performance loss' clause is untested because polysemanticity was never lowered.
No interpretation of mixed-response neurons is attempted.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied. The authors only argue that the class-based Mu basis may be too coarse.

missing.what: SAE-feature class-selectivity Mu across alpha (0.021, 0.021, 0.026; fraction > 0.5 is 0)
SAE L0 at alpha = 0.1 is 1306.4 (+32.5); PCA d95 drops 166.7 to 142.3

record.verdict_notes: The record's V3 links were removed: SAE L0 and dead-feature fraction on residual outputs are proxies for SAE-feature density, not tests that superposition causes neuron polysemanticity. The record's V5 'performance trade-off' label was dropped because no reduction in polysemanticity occurred. Tranche changed from T5 to T3: this is a new-setting null on one regularizer, not an argument that V5 is wrong.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures class-activation entropy, but does not identify neurons responding to semantically unrelated inputs or inspect examples such as cat faces and cars.
No language models or language-neuron measurements.
SAE L0 and dead-feature fraction are used as proxies for feature complexity; the study does not directly establish that features outnumber neurons or that capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
No test of initialization, training noise, or regularization producing polysemanticity when capacity is sufficient.
The tested intervention is TopoLoss in vision transformers. The study does not test SoLU, modern convnets, or other activation functions and regularizers.
The study does not interpret canonical mixed-activation neurons to determine whether their inputs share a feature or job.
It does not vary activation range or explanation-scoring method to test measurement dependence.

relation.reason: Its own Mu results across TopoLoss weights bear on V5's regularization clause.

tranche.reason: New setting (ViT-S/16 trained with TopoLoss on ImageNet-100) with its own result on whether a regularizer changes neuron selectivity (H1). It does not argue that V5 is wrong, so T5 does not fit.

source_check.notes: Mu is class-selectivity entropy over 100 ImageNet classes (higher means more selective). It is a proxy, not a share of polysemantic neurons, and the authors call H1 null overall. The Frac > 0.5 values (0.26/0.52/0.78%) equal 1, 2 and 3 of 384 sheet units, so the rise may be only a few neurons; the text gives no neuron count. SAE-feature Mu is also flat (Table 5), and TinyViT Mu is flat on a single seed (Table 9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: SAE L0 falls and dead-feature fraction rises relative to baseline, consistent with the paper's feature-complexity proxy for reduced superposition (r12, r15). The authors note an accuracy confound.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
